Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral hilar prominence and diffuse small nodular opacities, which corresponds to the classic radiographic presentation of sarcoidosis (bilateral symmetrical hilar lymphadenopathy with peribronchovascular nodules). This pattern helps distinguish it from lymphoma (typically unilateral or asymmetric masses) and tuberculosis (often associated with cavitation, effusion, or unilateral findings).
